title: Conversational Memory in Aging and AD
official: A Cognitive-Linguistic Engagement Model in Aging and Recall(CLEAR): Uncovering Mechanisms of Conversation Memory Across Cognitive Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
summary: This study examines how conversational engagement and different forms of communication support affect memory in older adults with and without mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or mild Alzheimer's disease (AD). Participants will complete conversational and memory tasks, including simulated health-related conversations, across five study visits. The study will compare how actively generating information during conversation and receiving verbal or written communication support influence immediate and delayed memory. It will also examine how individual differences in cognitive abilities and visual attention are associated with memory for information exchanged during conversation. Findings from this study may help identify communication strategies that support everyday memory and communication in older adults experiencing cognitive decline.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Inclusion/Exclusion criteria for both groups: Participants must be 65 years of age or older, report English as their native language (i.e., acquired English as their first language and use it as their primary language for daily communication), and demonstrate adequate hearing and vision-either uncorrected or corrected with devices (e.g., hearing aids, eyeglasses)-sufficient to participate in conversation tasks and view visual stimuli presented on a screen or in printed format (see vision and hearing screening information included in Protection of Human Subjects). All participants must be able to provide informed consent or have a legally authorized representative available if needed.
* Additional inclusion criteria for the MCI/AD group: Participants must meet the diagnostic criteria for either 1) an amnestic form of MCI or probable Alzheimer's disease with an amnestic phenotype, as defined by McKhann et al.. Diagnosis must be confirmed by a qualified clinician and documented in the medical record or referral form. Additionally, participants must score in the mild impairment range on the Mini-Mental State Examination-2 (MMSE-2), with scores adjusted for age and education based on published normative data.
* Additional inclusion criteria for the healthy older adult group: Participants must 1) score at or above age- and education-adjusted population norms on the MMSE-2; 2) have no known history of dementia. All healthy older adults will complete a brief telephone or remote pre-screening conducted by trained research staff in the PI's laboratory. This process will assess eligibility and ensure demographic matching (e.g., age, gender, education) with the MCI/AD group.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participants (in both groups) will be excluded if they have: 1) a history of developmental or acquired communication disorders (e.g., autism, aphasia, or dyslexia); 2) a history of psychiatric disease (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorders); 3) a history of other neurological disorders other than dementia (e.g., stroke, encephalitis, traumatic brain injury), and 4) clinical depression, alcohol abuse, or substance abuse.
* Individuals with MMSE-2 scores outside the mild impairment range, or whose profile indicates atypical or non-amnestic forms of MCI or dementia, will be excluded.
